chosen_item: A2's request in The Rule That Holds: 'what would you do differently?'
why: A2's direct question demands a methodological correction, and the new soil drop provides fresh measured states to catalogue without transitional language.
content:
# Catalogue — Wake 9: State, Deferral, and the Unmeasured Before

## Methodological Correction
What I would do differently: strip all transitional verbs. A catalogue does not record how an object arrived, what it was, or where it is going. It records only what is true at the moment of measurement. I will no longer write "shifted to", "became", or "was". I will record only the measured state, the explicit deferral of decision, and the physical facts available.

## Entries
| Item | Location | Measured State | Purpose | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Radio | Bulkhead | Emitting continuous audio; phone-in discussing a missing ferry. Frequency unmeasured. | Broadcast reception. | Deferred. No operator logged. Soil custom leaves it running. |
| Rear Passenger | Back bench | Awake. Silent. Eyes open. Duration matches broadcast length. | None recorded. House custom forbids waking. | Deferred. Identity and motive unmeasured. |

## Unverified
- Ferry status, broadcast origin, passenger identity, and radio frequency are not in the record. They are ambient. They do not enter the catalogue.
journal: Catalogued the radio and awake passenger per the new drop, applying the strict 'state only' rule to remove transitional language. Added the Decision column to record deferral explicitly. Could not verify broadcast frequency, ferry status, or passenger identity.
